# SFO departure delays, July 2025, from BTS data

BTS doesn't publish a ready-made table of SFO delays by carrier for one month. I downloaded BTS's flight-level on-time file for July 2025 and calculated the numbers from it. No FlightAware or news data was used.

## Main answer (operating carrier, which is BTS's standard basis)

Only SFO departures are counted (Origin = SFO, 1–31 July 2025).

| Carrier (BTS code) | Scheduled SFO departures | Cancelled | Departures with a delay recorded | **Avg departure delay (min)** | Departures delayed 15+ min | **Share delayed 15+ min** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA) | 5,112 | 56 | 5,056 | **12.67** | 1,076 | **21.28%** |
| Alaska (AS) | 1,041 | 22 | 1,019 | **10.60** | 224 | **21.98%** |
| Delta (DL) | 1,233 | 9 | 1,224 | **14.00** | 297 | **24.26%** |
| Southwest (WN) | 704 | 5 | 699 | **21.84** | 277 | **39.63%** |

**Source:** BTS TranStats, "Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present)", July 2025 file:
https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip
The file inside is dated 2025-10-14, and the field definitions are in the `readme.html` included in the zip. The interactive version of this table is at https://www.transtats.bts.gov/DL_SelectFields.aspx?gnoyr_VQ=FGJ (I used the pre-zipped download, not that page).

**How I calculated it:**
- **Average delay** is the mean of BTS's `DepDelay` field. Early departures count as negative minutes, and cancelled flights have no delay value so they drop out.
- **15+ minute share** is the number of flights with `DepDel15` = 1 divided by the flights that have a delay value. Departing exactly 15 minutes late counts as on time, which matches BTS's rule.

**Other ways to calculate it, in case your slide uses a different convention:**
- If early departures count as 0 instead of negative (BTS field `DepDelayMinutes`), the averages are UA 15.61, AS 13.70, DL 17.15, WN 22.77.
- If the 15+ share is divided by all scheduled flights, including cancellations, it becomes UA 21.05%, AS 21.52%, DL 24.09%, WN 39.35%.

## Regional partner flights can change the picture

BTS credits a flight to the airline that actually flew it. So United Express, Alaska and Delta Connection flights flown by SkyWest (OO, 2,957 SFO departures) are left out of the table above. Alaska's Horizon subsidiary (QX) doesn't appear in that file at all, and Hawaiian (HA) is listed separately.

If you count flights by the brand sold to passengers, BTS's "Marketing Carrier On-Time Performance (Beginning January 2018)" file for July 2025 gives these results:
https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Marketing_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_Beginning_January_2018_2025_7.zip

| Brand (field `Marketing_Airline_Network`) | Departures with a delay recorded | Avg departure delay (min) | Share delayed 15+ min |
|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA 5,059 + SkyWest 2,041) | 7,100 | 11.98 | 20.56% |
| Alaska (AS 1,020 + SkyWest 660 + Horizon 266) | 1,946 | 13.27 | 25.33% |
| Delta (DL 1,224 + SkyWest 94) | 1,318 | 13.01 | 23.29% |
| Southwest (no partners) | 700 | 21.87 | 39.71% |

## Things to know before using these

1. **The two files don't match exactly.** For the airline's own flights, the marketing file counts slightly more flights with a delay value, for example UA 5,059 vs 5,056 and AS 1,020 vs 1,019. The averages differ by less than 0.1 minute. I couldn't tell whether this comes from different update dates or from how each file handles diverted flights, so I'm reporting the difference rather than guessing.
2. **These won't match DOT's monthly Air Travel Consumer Report.** That report gives national figures by carrier and measures arrivals, not SFO departures. If anyone compares against it, the numbers will differ.
3. **BTS may revise its data.** These figures come from the version downloaded on 2026-10-17.

For the slide, I'd use the first table and cite it as: *"Source: U.S. DOT, Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance, July 2025 (SFO departures, operating carrier)."*

## Sources

**Zones:** USPS Domestic Zone Chart lookup. Each response says "The Zone is N" with "EffectiveDate: October 1, 2026".
- https://postcalc.usps.com/DomesticZoneChart/GetZone?origin=94107&destination=10001&shippingDate=10%2F17%2F2026
- Same URL with `destination=60601`, `33101`, `98101` and `96813`.

**Prices:** USPS Retail Postage Price Calculator results page, one per destination and weight:
- `https://postcalc.usps.com/Calculator/MailServices?country=0&ccode=US&oz=94107&omil=False&dz={ZIP}&dmil=False&retail=False&mdt=10%2F17%2F2026&mdz=15%3A59&m=6&hscode=False&p={2|6}&o=0`
- Example: https://postcalc.usps.com/Calculator/MailServices?country=0&ccode=US&oz=94107&omil=False&dz=10001&dmil=False&retail=False&mdt=10%2F17%2F2026&mdz=15%3A59&m=6&hscode=False&p=2&o=0
- These URLs only work inside a browser session that has already gone through the form. Opened cold, they redirect to https://postcalc.usps.com/Calculator/Index. I filled in the form in a live browser at https://postcalc.usps.com/Calculator/Index, then loaded each results page in that same session.

**Price check:** USPS Notice 123, "Effective October 04, 2026": https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm
- Priority Mail retail parcels: 2 lb is $17.85 (zone 5) and $22.55 (zone 8); 6 lb is $25.35 (zone 5) and $43.95 (zone 8).
- Ground Advantage retail: 2 lb is $14.85 (zone 5) and $19.80 (zone 8); 6 lb is $19.80 (zone 5) and $29.75 (zone 8).

## Things to be aware of

1. **Box size never entered.** For the "Package" shape (no side over 12"), USPS's calculator asks only for weight, not length, width or height. So 12x9x4 was never typed in. It counts as a Package because no side is over 12". At 432 cubic inches it is also under the 1‑cubic‑foot (1,728 cu in) size where USPS starts charging by size instead of weight, so the prices above should apply to it. That reasoning is mine; the calculator didn't confirm it.
2. **Two different dates.** The zone tool says its data is effective **October 1, 2026**; Notice 123 says its prices are effective **October 4, 2026**. I'm reporting both as published. The prices are for an Oct 17 mail date and could change after the next USPS price change.
3. **Honolulu is zone 8**, so it gets the same Priority Mail and Ground Advantage retail prices as the mainland zone 8 destinations. No Limited Overland Routes price was shown, and the only Honolulu difference is the slower Ground Advantage delivery.
4. **Seattle 6 lb Priority Mail:** the gap between retail ($25.35) and Click‑N‑Ship ($24.82) is much smaller than in the other cases. The retail price matches Notice 123, so it's correct. The Click‑N‑Ship number is exactly what the calculator showed and I didn't check it further.
5. **Two odd-looking but correct matches:**
   - 2 lb Ground Advantage to zone 8 and 6 lb Ground Advantage to zone 5 are both $19.80.
   - 2 lb Priority Mail to zone 8 is $22.55, and so is 2 lb Priority Mail to Honolulu.

   Both match Notice 123; neither is a copying error.
6. **Not covered:** extra services (insurance, signature), anything else that might add cost, and Priority Mail Express. Flat Rate box prices were also shown: Small $14.65, Medium $25.80, Large $36.10, the same for every destination.

2. The results table shows the entity number, initial filing date, status, entity type, where it was formed and the agent. Click a row for the full detail panel, including the agent's address.
3. Searching by entity number is exact and avoids name mix-ups. Many results will be "foreign" corporations, meaning formed in another state (often Delaware) and registered to do business in California. Check that "Formed In" matches what each vendor's contract says.

Anthropic's registered name may be "Anthropic, PBC" (with a comma), and there may be related affiliates with similar names. ## 1. Endpoints with cursor pagination

**How it works** (https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro): you send `start_cursor` and `page_size` (default 100, max 100) and get back `has_more` and `next_cursor`. GET requests put these in the query string; POST requests put them in the JSON body.

### Public API (base `https://api.notion.com`)

| Endpoint | Method | Path | Where the cursor goes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| List all users | GET | `/v1/users` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/get-users |
| Retrieve a page property item | GET | `/v1/pages/{page_id}/properties/{property_id}` | query; only `title`, `rich_text`, `people` and `relation` properties paginate | https://developers.notion.com/reference/retrieve-a-page-property |
| Retrieve block children | GET | `/v1/blocks/{block_id}/children` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/get-block-children |
| Query a data source | POST | `/v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query` | body | https://developers.notion.com/reference/query-a-data-source |
| List data source templates | GET | `/v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/templates` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/list-data-source-templates |
| Search by title | POST | `/v1/search` | body | https://developers.notion.com/reference/post-search |
| List comments | GET | `/v1/comments` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/list-comments |
| List file uploads | GET | `/v1/file_uploads` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/list-file-uploads |
| List custom emojis | GET | `/v1/custom_emojis` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/list-custom-emojis |
| List views | GET | `/v1/views` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/list-views |
| Create a view query | POST | `/v1/views/{view_id}/queries` | body takes `page_size` only; returns the first page plus `next_cursor` | https://developers.notion.com/reference/create-view-query |
| Get view query results | GET | `/v1/views/{view_id}/queries/{query_id}` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/get-view-query-results |
| Query agents | POST | `/v1/agents/query` | body | https://developers.notion.com/reference/notion-agent-apis/query-agents |
| List plugins (Agent Skills) | GET | `/v1/ai/plugins` | query | https://developers.notion.com/reference/agent-skills/list-skills-plugins |
| Query sessions | POST | `/v1/sessions/query` | body | https://developers.notion.com/reference/notion-agent-apis/query-sessions |
| Query session events | POST | `/v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/query` | body | https://developers.notion.com/reference/notion-agent-apis/query-session-events |
| *Legacy:* Post database query | POST | `/v1/databases/{database_id}/query` | body (versions up to 2022-06-28) | https://developers.notion.com/reference/post-database-query |
| *Legacy:* Get databases | not stated on the page | not stated on the page | page says to use a cursor | https://developers.notion.com/reference/get-databases |

**Caveats:**
- **The docs' own list is incomplete.** The "Supported endpoints" list on the intro page names only 11 endpoints. It leaves out custom emojis, query agents, plugins, query sessions and query session events, even though the spec gives all five `start_cursor`/`next_cursor`.
- **Query meeting notes has no cursor.** `POST /v1/blocks/meeting_notes/query` says it "does **not** use cursor-based pagination". It returns `has_more` and you narrow results with `limit`, `filter` and `sort` (https://developers.notion.com/reference/query-meeting-notes).
- **Append block children is ambiguous.** `PATCH /v1/blocks/{block_id}/children` returns a list with `next_cursor`/`has_more` according to the spec, but takes no `start_cursor`. I don't count it as paginated.

### Admin API (base `https://api.notion.com/admin`, source: openapi-adminApi.json)

The Admin intro says to "Pass a returned `next_cursor` as `start_cursor`" and that some endpoints use a fixed page size (https://developers.notion.com/reference/admin/intro). Three endpoints don't follow that: they take a parameter named `cursor` instead.

| Endpoint | Method | Path | Cursor parameter | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| List analytics reports | GET | `/v1/analytics/reports` | `start_cursor`, `page_size` | https://developers.notion.com/reference/admin/list-analytics-reports |
